chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'We do not know what to do with the people. If we narrate to them what we heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), they laugh, and if we remain silent, it is not bearable for us.'

He said, so Zamrah ibn Ma'bad said, 'Narrate to us.' So he said: 'Do you know what the enemy of Allah says when he is carried on his bier?' So we said, 'No.' He said: 'For he says to his bearers: Do you not hear that I am complaining to you? The enemy of Allah deceived me and imprisoned me, then did not release me. And I complain to you of brothers with whom I established brotherhood, so they abandoned me. And I complain to you of children whom I protected, so they abandoned me. And I complain to you of a house in which I spent my earnings, so its inhabitants became others than me. So be kind to me and do not hasten.'
He said, so Zamrah said, 'O Abu al-Hasan! If he speaks with this speech, he is likely to pounce upon the necks of those who carry him.'

He said, so Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah, if Zamrah has ridiculed the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then seize him with a seizure of grief/sorrow.'

He said, so he remained for forty days, then died, and a slave of his was present with him. He said, so when he was buried, Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) came to him and sat by him, and said to him, 'From where have you come, O so-and-so?' He said, 'From the funeral of Zamrah. I placed my face upon him when the soil was leveled over him, and I heard his voice. By Allah, I recognized it just as I recognized it when he was alive.'

'He was saying: Woe to you, O Zamrah ibn Ma'bad! Today every friend has abandoned you, and your destination has become the Hellfire, wherein is your dwelling, your overnight stay, and your daytime stay.'

He said, so Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said: 'I ask Allah for well-being. This is the recompense of the one who ridicules the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.سَرِيرِهِ: His bier/couch for carrying the dead
key_terms.ضَمْرَةُ بْنُ مَعْبَدٍ: Zamrah ibn Ma'bad, the companion who ridiculed hadith
key_terms.عَدُوُّ اللَّهِ: Enemy of Allah, a title often used for Zamrah in this context

ai.seo_question: What happened to Zamrah ibn Ma'bad after he ridiculed the hadith of the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of *al-tajassus* (spiritual inquiry) in the grave, where the deceased retains consciousness and communication with the living. Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) specifically links the ridicule of prophetic traditions to a loss of spiritual support, as Zamrah’s friends, family, and wealth—his worldly anchors—fail to aid him in the Hereafter. The narrative serves as a practical warning against dismissing religious knowledge, emphasizing that the grave is a place of reckoning where one’s relationship with the Ahl al-Bayt and the Prophet determines their fate.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir who said,

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> do not know how to deal with the people. If we narrate to them with what we<sup>asws</sup> heard from Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, they are laughing (in jest), and if we<sup>asws</sup> observe silence, we<sup>asws</sup> have no leeway (for that).

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Zamrato Bin Ma’bad said, ‘Narrate to us’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you know what the enemy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is saying when he is carried upon his coffin?’ So we said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So he is saying to his pallbearers, ‘Are you not hearing that I am complaining to you? The enemy of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> deceived me, and imprisoned me and did not release me. And I complain to you of brothers whom I established brotherhood with, so they abandoned me. I complain to you of children I protected, so they abandoned me. And I complain to you of a house which I spend upon my earning, so it became a dwelling for others. So, be kind to me and do not hasten.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So Zamrat said, ‘O Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>! If it was this speech he speaks with, (as if) he is about to pounce upon the necks of those that are carrying him’.

So Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! If it was so that Zamrat has ridiculed a Hadeeth of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so Seize him with an unfortunate Seizing’.

He (the narrator) said, So he remained for forty days, then died, and a slave of his was present with him. So when he had been buried, he came over to Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, and (after) offering a seat to him, Imam<sup>asws</sup> asked him: ‘Where are you coming from, O so and so?’ He said, ‘From the funeral of Zamrat, and I placed my face upon him when they evened (the soil) upon him, and I heard his voice. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I recognised it just as I had recognised it (beforehand) when he was alive.

He was saying, ‘O woe be unto you, O Zamrat Bin Ma’bad! Today every friend has abandoned you, and your destination has become the Blazing Fire wherein is you dwelling, and your overnight stay, and the daytime stay’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> ask Allah<sup>azwj</sup> for the well-being. This is a Recompense of the one who ridicules from the Ahadeeth of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir who has said the following:

“Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘We do not know how to deal with people. If we tell them that we have heard (such and such Hadith) from the Messenger of Allah, they laugh, and to remain silent (to neglect our mission) is not possible for us.’

The narrator has said that Damrah ibn Ma‘bad then said, ‘You then should narrate to us (of such) Ahadith.’ The Imam, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘Do you know what an enemy of Allah says when his body is placed on the stretcher?’ We replied, ’No, we do not know.’ The Imam then said, ’He says to those who carry his coffin, “Why is it that you do not listen to my complaints against Allah’s enemy who deceived me in taking me to wickedness and then did not help me to escape there-from? I complain before you against those with whom I established brotherly relations but they all betrayed me. I complain before you against the children whom I protected all the time but they also abandoned me. I complain before you against the house upon which I spent all my earnings but other people began to dwell therein. Please be kind and gentle to me and do not rush me up to my grave.’”
Damrah then said, ’O abu al-Hassan, if this man can say such things, he then may almost stand up on the shoulders of those who carry him.’
The narrator has said that Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘O Allah, if Damrah has made fun of Hadith of the Messenger of Allah, then hold him like an angry person does.’

The narrator has said that after forty days he died. He had a servant who after his burial came to Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He sat next to the Imam who asked, ‘Wherefrom are you coming O so and so?’ He replied, ’I have come from the burial of Damrah. I placed my face over him (his grave) when he was buried and I heard his voice which I recognized. It was just as I knew it was in his lifetime.

I heard him saying, “Woe is upon you, O Damrah ibn Ma’bad. Today all friends have abandoned you and your destination has become hell, wherein is your dwelling, a place of rest at night and in the morning.”
The narrator has said that Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘I plead before Allah for safety. Such is the recompense for those who make fun of the Ahadith of the Messenger of Allah.’”
